newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Uncertainty clouds Zaire peace talks in S.Africa.
newsitem.headline: Uncertainty clouds Zaire peace talks in S.Africa.

text.p: South Africa carried on with preparations on Friday for peace talks to try to settle the civil war in Zaire, but it was unclear whether they would go ahead on Saturday as expected.

The Zaire government's negotiating team was already in the country, meeting South African officials to discuss arrangements for the talks. But there was no official confirmation that representatives of the rebel side had arrived.
"From the government side everybody has arrived," a Zaire embassy spokesman said. "The starting date and location of the talks might be announced tomorrow."
Diplomatic sources, however, expressed some doubt.
They said Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko's appointment of opposition leader Etienne Tshisekedi as prime minister had complicated the situation on the eve of the proposed talks.
The new prime minister offered six key cabinet posts to the rebel movement of Laurent Kabila, who immediately rejected the gesture.
Tshisekedi also played down the importance of the proposed South Africa negotiations, saying Kabila was his brother and they did not need to talk through foreign intermediaries.

A plane carrying representatives of Kabila's Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire, led by foreign affairs commissioner Bizima Karaha, had been expected to arrive late on Thursday.
Local radio reports on Friday said the rebel team was in Johannesburg, but gave no sources and could not be confirmed.
